These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Convert amounts with to_money and ZERO: Wrap raw unit prices with ledgerly.money.to_money before arithmetic and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total do in ledgerly/invoice.py.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable codes: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with the established codes: `invalid_state` for wrong invoice status, `invalid_quantity` for bad quantities, `negative_amount` for negative money.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool from integer checks: When validating an integer argument, reject `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)`) because `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(x, int)`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

item.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc from clock
item.content: Use `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` to normalize any incoming datetime (e.g. `after`, `sub.started_at`) before comparing or doing arithmetic, so naive and aware datetimes are handled consistently.
